pack.name: Dhvani sample distress & scam reference pack
pack.authority: Operator-supplied demonstration reference pack. This is NOT an official police distress codebook. Replace or extend it with an authorised agency list before operational use.

entries.title: Request for help
entries.description: A direct request for assistance. Treat as a possible distress signal and review the surrounding audio and transcript before drawing conclusions.
entries.source_ref: Orbitwin sample reference pack v1.0, entry distress-help (operator-supplied; not an official codebook).

entries.title: Language indicating immediate danger
entries.description: Language that may indicate perceived immediate danger. This is a phrase match, not proof that a crime is occurring.
entries.source_ref: Orbitwin sample reference pack v1.0, entry distress-danger (operator-supplied; not an official codebook).

entries.title: Emergency number 112 mentioned
entries.description: The national emergency number in India. Verify whether the caller was referring to the emergency service or reading a number in another context.
entries.source_ref: Government of India emergency response number 112 (public information).

entries.title: Digital arrest
entries.description: A fraud pattern in which callers impersonate police, CBI or customs officials and claim an arrest is taking place over a video call. Genuine agencies do not conduct arrests or evidence verification in this way. Treat the phrase as a lead for review, not as proof of a crime.
entries.source_ref: Government of India Cyber Crime Portal awareness material: https://cybercrime.gov.in/

entries.title: Customs / courier parcel scam
entries.description: A fraud narrative claiming that a parcel in the victim's name contains illegal goods and that payment or verification is required. Verify through the courier or customs authority using independently sourced contact details.
entries.source_ref: Government of India Cyber Crime Portal awareness material: https://cybercrime.gov.in/

entries.title: Mule account
entries.description: An account used to receive or move criminal proceeds. Fraudsters may ask a victim or recruit to transfer money through such an account. A mention is a lead, not proof of criminal conduct.
entries.source_ref: Reserve Bank of India consumer awareness material and Government of India Cyber Crime Portal: https://cybercrime.gov.in/

entries.title: OTP / credential request
entries.description: A request for a one-time password, PIN or card verification value. Legitimate staff do not need these secrets to help a customer. Treat the request as a potential fraud indicator and never repeat the secret in a report.
entries.source_ref: Reserve Bank of India consumer awareness material: https://www.rbi.org.in/

entries.title: Claimed police / CBI verification
entries.description: A claimed official identity or verification procedure. Independently verify the caller through an official published number. This phrase alone does not establish impersonation.
entries.source_ref: Government of India Cyber Crime Portal awareness material: https://cybercrime.gov.in/

entries.title: Urgent payment or transfer demand
entries.description: A demand for an urgent payment or transfer. Payment pressure can occur in legitimate disputes too; review the full conversation and verify the recipient independently.
entries.source_ref: Orbitwin sample reference pack v1.0, entry scam-payment (operator-supplied; not an official codebook).

entries.title: Potentially controlling language
entries.description: Language that may indicate someone is being discouraged from speaking or seeking help. This is a contextual lead only and is not proof of coercion, kidnapping or guilt.
entries.source_ref: Orbitwin sample reference pack v1.0, entry context-control (operator-supplied; not an official codebook).
